full_judgment: 2. The plaintiff-petitioner instituted the aforesaid suit for declaration and permanent injunction upon the averments that the petitioner as the mutwalli of two waqf estates created by his great grandfather late Chowdhury Raisuddin Ahmed Siddiky and his grand-father late Khan Bahadur Kasemuddin Ahmed Siddiky unsuccessfully challenged by Writ Petition No. 80 of 1957 the general Notification, Nos. 4836-L.R. and 4849-L.R. both dated 2.4.56 purporting to acquire en block with effect from 14.4.56 all the remaining rent-receiving interest in the District of Dhaka under section 3(1) and all khas lands under section 3(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Thereafter on 24.5.60 Ordinance No. IX of 1960 was promulgated amending the said Act by adding a new section l0A and on 7.2.62 Ordinance No.IV of 1962 was promulgated providing, inter alia, that the then Provincial Government having not exercised the right of possession in respect of waqf and debuttor interests after the aforesaid notification, the mutwalli or shebait shall continue and be deemed to have continued to manage such interests as the agent of the then Provincial Government till the last day of the agricultural year next following the date of publication of the notification under section 43(2) of the Act declaring that Compensation Assessment Roll in respect of such interest has been finally published. It is the plaintiffs contention that the Compensation Assessment Roll in respect of the two waqf estates in question have not been prepared in accordance with the terms of the said Act and the rules framed thereunder. The plaintiff has given particulars of non-compliance of the Act and the rules. He stated that he was still in undisturbed and unhampered possession of all the properties of the concerned waqf estates as mutwalli even after the aforesaid general notification by realising rents and tolls, except the forest lands described in schedule -III of the plaint. When the plaintiffs possession was threatened by the officers of the defendant No.1, the then Province of East Pakistan, the plaintiff again filed Writ Petition No.146 of 1964, but a Special Bench of the High Court of East Pakistan discharged the Rule on 7.4.65 by a majority decision holding that the plaintiffs waqf estates stood acquired under the notifications dated 2.4.56. The plaintiff preferred Civil Appeal No. 27-D of 1965 in the then Supreme Court of Pakistan and obtained an order of stay on 15.8.65. The appeal was dismissed by the Supreme Court of Pakistan on 26.2.68 with the observation, inter alia, that if there be any defect in the proceedings which culminated in the publication of the Compensation Assessment Rolls, then it would still be open to the plaintiff-petitioner to agitate the matter in the proper forum.
